# 842 — Every First Residual Polar Collision Is Generated by Its Existing Normal Map

## Residual supports

Entry 840 leaves three loci where its diagonal/anti-diagonal determinant
vanishes:

\[
P_3=0,\qquad a=0,\qquad b=0.
\]

On each divisor, the labelled factors \(Q_+\) and \(Q_-\) have the same
restriction. Their normal derivatives are opposite.

## Soft \(P_3\) divisor

At \(P_3=0\),

\[
Q_+=Q_-
=E^2(a^2-b^2)-P_1^2a^2+P_2^2b^2,
\]

while

\[
\left(\partial_{P_3}Q_+,\partial_{P_3}Q_-\right)
=2Eab(1,-1).
\]

The restriction/normal determinant is \(-4Eab\).

## Coordinate divisors

At \(a=0\),

\[
Q_+=Q_-=b^2(P_2^2-E^2),
\qquad
\left(\partial_aQ_+,\partial_aQ_-\right)
=2EP_3b(1,-1),
\]

with determinant \(-4EP_3b\).

At \(b=0\),

\[
Q_+=Q_-=a^2(E^2-P_1^2),
\qquad
\left(\partial_bQ_+,\partial_bQ_-\right)
=2EP_3a(1,-1),
\]

with determinant \(-4EP_3a\).

## Consequence

On every first residual divisor, ordinary restriction supplies the
diagonal line and the predeclared soft or coordinate normal map supplies
the anti-diagonal line. Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\dim\operatorname{Cone}=0
}
\]

generically on each divisor.

The determinants fail only on pairwise or deeper intersections among

\[
E,\qquad P_3,\qquad a,\qquad b.
\]

No new failure divisor has appeared. The next audit is finite: totalize
the resulting four-coordinate incidence cube and test whether its
alternating Čech/Koszul differential leaves any corner cohomology.
